tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

<style>

  canvas { display: block; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; }

{ "imports": {
  "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<email>/build/three.module.js",

import { EffectComposer } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js';
import { RenderPass } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/RenderPass.js';
import { UnrealBloomPass } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/UnrealBloomPass.js';
import { ShaderPass } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/ShaderPass.js';
import { OutputPass } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/OutputPass.js';

/*
  10-second loop, every motion is a pure function of t in [0,10):
   0.0 - 3.0  neon solar system in orbit
   3.0 - 6.0  gravitational implosion: everything spirals into the sun
   6.0        singularity flash + shockwave
   6.0 - 9.8  nova rebirth: particles burst out, overshoot, settle on their orbits
  Orbital phases are made loop-exact by folding the leftover angle into the implosion swirl.
*/
const LOOP = 10, TAU = Math.PI * 2;
const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const frozenT = params.has('t') ? parseFloat(params.get('t')) : null;

// ---------- renderer / scene ----------
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance' });
renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2));
renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight);
renderer.setClearColor(0x020008, 1);
renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping;
renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.05;
document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);

const scene = new THREE.Scene();
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(50, innerWidth / innerHeight, 0.1, 2000);

// ---------- deterministic random ----------
let seed = 1337;
const rnd = () => { seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647; return (seed - 1) / 2147483646; };
const gauss = () => Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(rnd() + 1e-9)) * Math.cos(TAU * rnd());
const unit = () => { const z = rnd() * 2 - 1, a = rnd() * TAU, s = Math.sqrt(1 - z * z); return [s * Math.cos(a), z, s * Math.sin(a)]; };
const col = h => { const c = new THREE.Color(h); return [c.r, c.g, c.b]; };

  const extraTurns = Math.round(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(14 / r, 1, 3));

// Asteroid belt
for (let i = 0; i < 16000; i++) {

  add({ r, a0: rnd() * TAU, local: [0, gauss() * 0.8, 0], color: mixc(col('#00e5ff'), col('#5b2bff'), rnd()), size: 0.1, kind: 3, incl: 0.03, node: 2.0 });

// ---------- shared shader code ----------
const common = /* glsl */`
  uniform float uTime;
  uniform float uProj;
  attribute vec4 aOrbit; attribute vec3 aLocal; attribute vec3 aDir;
  attribute vec3 aColor; attribute vec4 aMisc; attribute vec3 aTilt;
  const float TAU = 6.28318530718; const float PI = 3.14159265359; const float LOOP = 10.0;
  float smoother(float x){ x = clamp(x,0.,1.); return x*x*x*(x*(x*6.-15.)+10.); }
  mat3 rotY(float a){ float c=cos(a), s=sin(a); return mat3(c,0.,-s, 0.,1.,0., s,0.,c); }
  mat3 rotX(float a){ float c=cos(a), s=sin(a); return mat3(1.,0.,0., 0.,c,s, 0.,-s,c); }

  // position of this particle at loop time t; heat 0..1, phase 0 = implosion side, 1 = rebirth side
  vec3 sysPos(float t, out float heat, out float side){
    float r = aOrbit.x, a0 = aOrbit.y, w = aOrbit.z, R = aOrbit.w;
    float delay = aMisc.z, kind = aMisc.w;
    float s = smoother((t - 3.0 - delay*0.9) / 5.7);
    float ang = a0 + w*t + R*s;

    float tStart = 3.0 + delay*1.5;
    float ti = clamp((t - tStart) / (6.0 - tStart), 0., 1.);
    float c = ti*ti*ti;
    float u = clamp((t - 6.0) / (3.0 + delay*0.8), 0., 1.);
    float f, scatter = 0.;
    if (t < 6.0) { f = 1.0 - c; heat = c; side = 0.; }
    else { float v = 1.0 - u; f = 1.0 - v*v*v*cos(3.0*PI*u); heat = v*v; side = 1.; scatter = pow(sin(PI*u), 2.0); }

    vec3 center = vec3(cos(ang)*r, 0., sin(ang)*r);
    center = rotY(aTilt.y) * (rotX(aTilt.x) * (rotY(-aTilt.y) * center));

    float spin = aTilt.z * TAU * t / LOOP + TAU * 2.0 * s;
    vec3 loc = rotY(spin) * aLocal;
    if (kind < 0.5) { // boiling sun surface, periodic in t
      float ph = TAU * t / LOOP;
      float b = sin(dot(aLocal, vec3(2.1,1.7,1.3)) + ph*3.0) * sin(dot(aLocal, vec3(-1.3,2.4,0.7)) - ph*2.0);
      loc *= 1.0 + 0.09*b;
    }
    vec3 p = center + loc;
    float tw = c*(1.0-c)*4.0;
    p.y += sin(ang*3.0 + aMisc.y*TAU) * tw * (r*0.10 + 0.6);
    p *= f;
    p += aDir * (0.55 * pow(heat, 6.0));            // finite-size singularity core
    p += aDir * scatter * (r*0.32 + 4.0);           // nova burst shell
    return p;
  }
  vec3 heatColor(float heat, float side){
    vec3 hotIn  = mix(vec3(1.0,0.15,0.75), vec3(1.0,0.95,1.0), heat*heat);
    vec3 hotOut = mix(vec3(0.2,0.85,1.0), vec3(1.0,1.0,1.0), heat*heat);
    vec3 hot = mix(hotIn, hotOut, side);
    return mix(aColor, hot, smoothstep(0.0, 0.9, heat));
  }
`;

const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
const f32 = a => new Float32Array(a);
geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(count * 3), 3));

const uniforms = { uTime: { value: 0 }, uProj: { value: 1 }, uFlash: { value: 0 } };

const pointsMat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
  uniforms,
  vertexShader: common + /* glsl */`
    varying vec3 vColor; varying float vAlpha;
    void main(){
      float heat, side;
      vec3 p = sysPos(uTime, heat, side);
      vec4 mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(p, 1.0);
      gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;
      float kind = aMisc.w;

  fragmentShader: /* glsl */`

// ---------- motion streaks: line segments from p(t-dt) to p(t) ----------
{
  const pick = [];
  const misc = A.misc;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) if (misc[i * 4 + 3] > 0.5 && rnd() < 0.22) pick.push(i);
  const n = pick.length * 2;
  const lg = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
  const names = { aOrbit: 4, aLocal: 3, aDir: 3, aColor: 3, aMisc: 4, aTilt: 3 };
  const src = { aOrbit: A.orbit, aLocal: A.local, aDir: A.dir, aColor: A.color, aMisc: A.misc, aTilt: A.tilt };
  for (const [name, sz] of Object.entries(names)) {
    const out = new Float32Array(n * sz);
    pick.forEach((idx, j) => { for (let e = 0; e < 2; e++) for (let k = 0; k < sz; k++) out[(j * 2 + e) * sz + k] = src[name][idx * sz + k]; });
    lg.setAttribute(name, new THREE.BufferAttribute(out, sz));
  }
  const tail = new Float32Array(n); for (let j = 0; j < pick.length; j++) tail[j * 2 + 1] = 1;
  lg.setAttribute('aTail', new THREE.BufferAttribute(tail, 1));
  lg.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(n * 3), 3));

  const lineMat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({

// ---------- background stars ----------
{
  const n = 7000, pos = new Float32Array(n * 3), c = new Float32Array(n * 3), r = new Float32Array(n);

// ---------- billboard glow: sun halo + singularity flash with anamorphic streak ----------
const glowU = { uSun: { value: 1 }, uFlash: uniforms.uFlash, uAspect: { value: 1 } };
const glow = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2, 2), new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
  uniforms: glowU,
  vertexShader: /* glsl */`
    varying vec2 vP;
    void main(){
      vP = position.xy;
      vec4 mv = viewMatrix * vec4(0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0);
      mv.xy += position.xy * 60.0;
      gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;
    }`,
  fragmentShader: /* glsl */`
    uniform float uSun, uFlash; varying vec2 vP;
    void main(){

const smoother = x => { x = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, x)); return x * x * x * (x * (x * 6 - 15) + 10); };

}
function update(t) {
  uniforms.uTime.value = t;
  const fl = flashAt(t);
  uniforms.uFlash.value = fl;
  // sun presence: shrinks with the implosion, reborn after
  const sunCollapse = t < 6 ? Math.pow(smoother((t - 4.0) / 2.0), 2) : 1 - smoother((t - 6.5) / 2.8);
  glowU.uSun.value = 1 - sunCollapse;
  shockU.uShock.value = t >= 6 ? (t - 6) / 2.6 : -1;

  const env = t < 6 ? smoother((t - 2.8) / 3.2) : 1 - smoother((t - 6.2) / 3.6);
  const T = TAU * t / LOOP;
  const az = 0.7 + 0.55 * Math.sin(T) + 0.35 * env;
  const el = 0.5 + 0.1 * Math.sin(2 * T + 1.0) - 0.12 * env;
  const dist = 74 - 30 * env;
  const shakeA = t > 6 ? Math.exp(-(t - 6) * 5) * 0.9 : 0;
  camera.position.set(
    dist * Math.cos(el) * Math.sin(az) + shakeA * Math.sin(t * 97),
    dist * Math.sin(el) + shakeA * Math.sin(t * 71 + 1),
    dist * Math.cos(el) * Math.cos(az));
  camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0);
  camera.rotateZ(0.12 * Math.sin(T) + env * 0.15);

  bloom.strength = 1.0 + 1.4 * fl + 0.4 * env;
  bloom.radius = 0.55 + 0.25 * fl;
  finish.uniforms.uAb.value = fl + env * 0.3;
  finish.uniforms.uTime.value = t;
}

const t0 = performance.now();

addEventListener('keydown', e => {

  const t = frozenT !== null ? ((frozenT % LOOP) + LOOP) % LOOP : (ms / 1000) % LOOP;
  update(t);
  composer.render();
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}

content.text:
I've built the animation as a single web page at **<workspace>/.ambition/direct/index.html**. I checked it with headless-Chromium screenshots across the whole loop and on a phone-sized screen. Open it in a browser; it loads three.js from a CDN, so it needs internet. I haven't measured the frame rate on a real graphics card, because the headless browser renders in software.

**What it does:** about 250,000 glowing particles make up a neon sun, 8 planets (Saturn with rings, Earth with a moon), orbit lines, an asteroid belt and outer dust.
- **0–3 s:** the system orbits normally.
- **3–6 s:** everything spirals into the sun, leaving motion streaks and turning hot magenta.
- **6 s:** it collapses to a single point that flashes white with a horizontal lens streak, and three neon shockwave rings spread out.
- **6–10 s:** particles burst outward, overshoot, and settle back onto their orbits.

Every position, colour and camera move is calculated from time modulo 10 seconds, so the loop has no visible seam. Bloom and slight colour fringing add the neon glow, and the framing adjusts on portrait screens. Space pauses it, and adding `?t=5.5` to the address freezes it on one moment.

**How I checked it:**
- **Screenshots at key moments:** I captured frames at 0, 2, 4, 5, 5.8, 6.05, 6.5, 7, 7.6, 8.5, 9.3 and 9.99 s. The first versions were badly overexposed: from the implosion onward the frames were mostly white. Two of the shaders also used a function in a way that isn't reliably supported. I fixed both, re-captured, and looked at every frame again.
- **The loop seam:** I compared the frames at 0 s and 9.999 s pixel by pixel. They differ by only 2.15 out of 255 on average, which is mostly the deliberate film grain.
- **Phone screen:** I rendered it at 390×844 and confirmed it runs with no console errors.

One thing that still isn't ideal: the two largest planets glow almost white rather than in colour as they're pulled in, around the 5-second mark.

The screenshot and comparison scripts are in /tmp/pwtool, outside the work folder.
